description: Historical and Design Storm Precipitation Profiles for Lucknow (IMD Records & CPHEEO Standards)

scenarios.name: 14 Sept 2023 Historic Cloudburst
scenarios.news_reference: Times of India & Amar Ujala: 160 mm rain in 24 hrs brings Lucknow to standstill, schools closed, hospitals flooded
scenarios.description: Extreme convective thunderstorm that caused knee-to-waist-deep inundation in Hazratganj, Charbagh, Gomti Nagar, and Aliganj.

scenarios.name: 18 Aug 2026 Monsoon Surge
scenarios.news_reference: Times of India (Aug 18, 2026): Intermittent rain disrupts city, Nirala Nagar, Jankipuram, and Gomti Nagar inundated
scenarios.description: Prolonged monsoon downpour overwhelming local branch drains and causing widespread traffic stranding across trans-Gomti.

scenarios.name: 28 July 2021 High-Intensity Flash Flood
scenarios.news_reference: Hindustan Times: 114 mm torrential downpour submerges Charbagh Railway station and Old City under 2 feet of water
scenarios.description: Sudden cloudburst-grade event with peak intensity reaching 85 mm/hr in the second 15-minute interval.

scenarios.name: Standard Municipal Design Baseline
scenarios.news_reference: CPHEEO Manual on Storm Water Drainage Systems (Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Govt of India)
scenarios.description: Standard 15 mm/hr steady design storm used for baseline pipe dimensioning across Indian municipal corporations.

scenarios.name: Moderate Monsoon Shower (2x Design)
scenarios.news_reference: Moderate monsoon rain event testing conveyance limits of branch drains
scenarios.description: Typical monsoon shower exceeding branch pipe capacity and beginning surface ponding in low depressions.

scenarios.name: Heavy Downpour (4x Design)
scenarios.news_reference: Heavy storm triggering emergency alert level
scenarios.description: Heavy severe rain triggering full trunk capacity surcharge and street waterlogging across low-lying roads.

scenarios.name: Extreme Cloudburst (6.7x Design)
scenarios.description: Disaster-level cloudburst event overwhelming all municipal drainage infrastructure and causing major road blockages.
